title: Flexible Sprint Shelving & Swapboard for Capacity Rebalancing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Create an operational playbook and lightweight tooling pattern to temporarily 'shelve' noncritical planned work and redeploy engineers into a short-term Swapboard when mid-cycle load spikes occur. The goal is to reduce fire-drill churn, preserve critical-path momentum, and standardize decisions for scope cuts and temporary reallocation across PM/Eng/Design.

Background: We frequently see midcycle bursts from incidents, large customer onboarding, or sales-driven deadlines. Current ad-hoc reassignments cause single-threading, unclear ownership, and missed expectations. Instead of broad scope cuts, the Sprint Shelving + Swapboard pattern provides a reversible, timeboxed way to park work and create staffed surge lanes with explicit acceptance criteria.

Proposed mechanism: 
1) Sprint Shelf: a curated list of tickets (<= 10% of cycle capacity) that can be paused with documented state (pending QA, blocked on infra, design polish). Each shelved ticket stores required rehydration steps.
2) Swapboard: a short roster of engineers (2-6 people) who opt into temporary surge roles for a 1-2 week window. Swapboard members pick from a small menu: incident triage, onboarding automation, dedicated rollout support, or high-priority bug hunts.
3) Decision gates: PM leads own which tickets are eligible for shelving. An on-duty triage panel (PM + Eng lead + Design lead) approves Swapboard activation if surge metrics exceed thresholds.
4) Reversion: Shelved tickets have a fixed shelf window and explicit re-evaluation date. Reassignment back to owners happens automatically outside surge windows.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Documented Sprint Shelf rubric and Swapboard roster template published in Confluence.
- A pilot with 2 teams runs for one cycle and logs reassign/rehydration times.
- A measurable reduction in hot-reassign incidents (target: -30% midcycle) for pilot teams.

Success metrics: 
- Time-to-recover for shelved tickets after rehydration (median target < 5 working days).
- Number of unplanned handoffs per surge event (target < 2).
- Stakeholder satisfaction score collected via post-cycle survey (target >= 4/5).

Risks & trade-offs: 
- Risk of perceived backlog deprioritization by teams; mitigated via mandatory re-evaluation and visibility dashboards.
- Potential over-use of Swapboard leading to repeated interrupts for same engineers; mitigated via rotation caps and opt-out windows.
- Administrative overhead in tracking shelved work; we recommend initially manual tracking (sheet + labels) before investing in tooling.

Rollout plan: 
- Week 1: Draft rubric and roster template; share with engineering managers for feedback.
- Week 2: Pilot with Platform infra and Runtime teams; use manual Google Sheet and GitHub label convention (label: "shelf/pending-swap").
- Week 3-4: Collect metrics, iterate rubric, make small automation in triage bot to tag re-evaluate dates.
- Post-pilot: Decide on full adoption and console/Linear integration work.

Monitoring & dashboards: Add short-term dashboard widgets: surge trigger rate, Swapboard utilization, shelved-ticket count, rehydration lag. Dashboard source: "SurgeOps - Cycle Health" in internal metrics cluster.

Owner & stakeholders: PM owner: Aisha Patel. Engineering leads: Marco Reyes (Platform), Linh Tran (Runtime). Design review: Sophie Laurent. Legal/compliance: notified for private deployment customers (if surge impacts dedicated/enterprise commitments).
